A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work by Jeong and Townsend. Their text, equations, numerical figures and complete Appendices A–B support reliable comparison despite substantial reformatting.

before.justification: Figures 1–2 report numerical computations of kernel approximation errors, including the tanh(100xy+1) example with 96 selected pivots.

after.justification: Figures 1–2 retain these numerical results. Section 5.1 explicitly describes applying the algorithm to the tanh kernel and obtaining a 96-pivot approximation.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the same pseudo-skeleton approximation using Gaussian elimination with complete pivoting, followed by functional QR, a small matrix SVD and truncation. The added attribution does not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Both use the same two tent-type kernels and tanh(100xy+1) on [-1,1] squared. The expanded discussion of Transformers, control and biological sequences introduces no evaluations in those domains.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains the Legendre-based bound and best-rank approximation error comparison; Figure 2 retains pseudo-skeleton error versus best-rank error. No evaluated comparator is added or removed.

E3.justification: The kernel domains, L2 error measures, rank sweeps and adaptive approximation procedure remain unchanged. No new evaluation protocol or revised experimental setting is reported.

E4.justification: Figures 1–2 retain the same examinations of approximation-bound tightness and pseudo-skeleton accuracy. The appendices retain theoretical proofs, with no added ablations, robustness tests or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run statistics, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The numerical illustrations introduce no changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: The plotted errors and trends in Figures 1–2 are retained, including the 96-pivot tanh approximation. Section 4 adds a pointer to prior numerical experiments without adding local results.

T1.justification: Equation (3) adds absolute values around both partial derivatives, correcting the displayed bounded-variation condition from signed derivative integrals to integrals of derivative magnitudes. The theorem statements, decay derivations and proofs in Appendices A–B are otherwise retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1 and conclusion retain the same contributions: convergence counterexamples, convergence guarantees under uniform bounded variation, singular-value decay bounds and an algorithm for computing the expansion.

C2.justification: Section 3.4 newly discusses the restriction to real domains and cancellation as an obstacle to broader extensions. Section 2.2 adds a qualification about converting indefinite kernels to positive-definite ones. These expand the interpretation and applicability discussion.

D1.justification: The Chebfun implementation reference, adaptive Chebyshev sampling, tolerance example and computational complexity are retained. Added pointers to specific figures in previously cited works disclose no new implementation settings or code/data access.

R1.justification: Adds references to Chen et al. (2024), Cortes and Vapnik (1995), Hassibi et al. (1999), Scholkopf and Smola (2002), and Vert et al. (2004). Section 5 more explicitly attributes the existing computational algorithm to Townsend and Trefethen.

P1.justification: Limited paragraph additions clarify applications, domain restrictions and attribution, and the duplicated word in the Section 3.4.2 heading is removed. The overall section order and appendix organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The entire document adopts an ICLR conference layout, changing typography, the title/author block, headings, running headers, equation-number placement and caption formatting. Figure 2 moves within Section 5, while both figures retain their plotted content.

improvement.justification: v2 corrects the missing absolute values in the central bounded-variation condition, explicitly discusses limits of extending the theory to broader domains, and clarifies algorithm attribution. These provide focused gains in mathematical precision and positioning while retaining the principal results, numerical evidence and appendix proofs.
